question: A community nurse is mapping health risks in a rural village. What is the best way to find pregnant teenage brides?

options.A: Reviewing national census reports published every ten years
options.B: Partnering with local women leaders and tracking school dropout patterns
options.C: Waiting in urban tertiary hospitals for emergency referrals to arrive
options.D: Relying solely on self-reporting via digital mobile phone surveys

explanation: Local women leaders and school attendance logs give nurses the best grassroots view of which young girls are dropping out and entering marriages. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T6#GNS225_U6_T6_h6)

question: Which of these is a direct medical cost in patient care?

options.A: Emotional distress experienced by family members
options.B: Hospital room charges and nursing care
options.C: Bus fare paid by a patient traveling to the clinic
options.D: Lost wages due to missing work while sick

explanation: Direct medical costs are the actual bills for clinical services and treatments—like your room, drugs, and nursing care. [learn more](GST322_U2_T5#GST322_U2_T5_h2)

question: A remote Nigerian village has no government clinic and relies heavily on a local mission hospital for maternity care. What type of organization is running this hospital?

options.A: Commercial pharmaceutical firm
options.B: Faith-Based Organization
options.C: Advocacy NGO
options.D: Global regulatory body

explanation: Mission hospitals run by religious groups are faith-based organizations, and they play a massive role in bringing healthcare to rural communities. [learn more](GST322_U4_T12#GST322_U4_T12_h2)

question: Why is it smart to check that gas is actually flowing out of the cannula prongs before placing them on the patient?

options.A: To measure the exact oxygen percentage in the room air
options.B: To confirm the equipment works and gas is actively delivering
options.C: To clear out any trapped dust from the manufacturing factory
options.D: To warm up the cold gas before it touches the sensitive nasal lining

explanation: A quick check saves a lot of trouble—you want to make sure there isn't a kinked tube or a closed valve blocking air before it reaches your patient. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T9#GNS212_U2_T9_h4)

question: What do we call an opportunistic infection?

options.A: A severe infection that only affects individuals over the age of sixty-five
options.B: An illness caused by bacteria that cannot survive outside a host body
options.C: An infection caused by normal flora when the host's defenses are weakened
options.D: A disease spread exclusively through contaminated hospital water supplies

explanation: Think of it this way: normal microbes are usually peaceful neighbours, but if your immune system gets weak, they 'take the opportunity' to cause trouble and sickness. [learn more](GST114_U3_T1#GST114_U3_T1_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a safe practice in food distribution?

options.A: Packing food items inside old fertilizer sacks
options.B: Protecting perishable produce from exhaust fumes and dust
options.C: Washing and sanitizing loading compartments regularly
options.D: Using clean, dedicated food-grade transport vehicles

explanation: Fertilizer sacks can transfer harmful chemical residues directly into consumable foods, posing a serious health hazard. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T025#GNS227_U2_T025_h6)

question: A community nurse sets up a free blood pressure check station in the local market. What level of prevention is this?

options.A: Secondary prevention
options.B: Primary prevention
options.C: Quaternary prevention
options.D: Tertiary prevention

explanation: You're doing great! Screening checks (like blood pressure tests) catch problems early so treatment can start before things get worse. That is secondary prevention. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T1#GNS225_U2_T1_h3)

question: What is the normal baseline range for the fetal heart rate?

options.A: 60 to 100 beats per minute
options.B: 110 to 160 beats per minute
options.C: 80 to 120 beats per minute
options.D: 140 to 180 beats per minute

explanation: A healthy baseline fetal heart rate consistently falls between 110 and 160 beats per minute during labor. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h4)

question: A nurse sets up a desk in the village square to check blood sugar levels for healthy adults. What level of prevention is this?

options.A: Tertiary prevention
options.B: Primary prevention
options.C: Quaternary prevention
options.D: Secondary prevention

explanation: You nailed it! Screening tests catch health issues early before big symptoms show up, which is what secondary prevention is all about. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T8#GNS225_U1_T8_h3)

question: What does the term 'intersectionality' mean in healthcare?

options.A: The intersection of rural roads leading to a clinic
options.B: A meeting point between doctors and community leaders
options.C: How gender overlaps with poverty, age, and disability
options.D: The physical crossing of blood vessels in the heart

explanation: Intersectionality simply means looking at the whole person—how things like gender, age, and poverty combine to create unique challenges. Great concept to know as a nurse! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T22#GNS225_U5_T22_h6)

question: Why is a patient taking long-term steroid medications at a higher risk of getting infections?

options.A: Corticosteroids cause an immediate permanent loss of lymph nodes
options.B: The medication suppresses normal immune and inflammatory responses
options.C: The treatment increases the production of abnormal red blood cells
options.D: The drug directly destroys the protective outer layers of the skin

explanation: Spot on! Corticosteroids calm down inflammation, but in doing so, they also quiet down the immune system, making it harder to fight off everyday germs. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T2#GNS123_U4_T2_h6)

question: Why do modern healthcare facilities promote a blame-free reporting culture for medication errors?

options.A: It encourages open reporting to identify system flaws and prevent future errors
options.B: It reduces the need for expensive hospital legal representation
options.C: It ensures that nurses never have to face consequences for careless mistakes
options.D: It speeds up the process of discharging patients from the hospital

explanation: When staff feel safe from unfair punishment, they report mistakes honestly, allowing the team to fix underlying system weaknesses. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T2#GNS125_U4_T2_h8)

question: What is a major advantage of DOACs (like rivaroxaban) over old-school warfarin?

options.A: They do not require routine blood tests to monitor the INR
options.B: They are completely safe to use in patients with severe kidney failure
options.C: They work instantly by dissolving existing blood clots in veins
options.D: They have zero risk of bleeding complications whatsoever

explanation: Patients love DOACs because they can skip the frequent clinic visits for INR blood draws while still staying protected! [learn more](GNS223_U1_T5#GNS223_U1_T5_h5)

question: Why do standard primary health clinics often struggle to attract young people?

options.A: They charge higher fees for younger patients.
options.B: They only open during school hours.
options.C: They refuse to treat patients without a parent present.
options.D: They are usually structured for either small children or older adults.

explanation: Traditional clinics are often set up for babies (immunizations) or older adults, leaving teenagers feeling awkward and out of place. Great clinics need to feel welcoming to everyone! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T48#GNS214_U1_T48_h1)

question: What triggers the cough and breathing issues in the early stage of ascariasis?

options.A: Allergic reaction to the toxins produced in the stomach
options.B: Larvae migrating through the lung tissue and alveoli
options.C: Adult worms pressing upward against the diaphragm
options.D: Secondary bacterial pneumonia caused by poor hygiene

explanation: As the tiny larvae travel through the lungs, they cause irritation and inflammation, leading to a cough that can mimic pneumonia. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T22#GNS313_U2_T22_h3)

question: What often happens over time if juvenile delinquency is left unaddressed?

options.A: Automatic entry into high-ranking government leadership roles
options.B: Transition into chronic adult criminal behavior and incarceration
options.C: Spontaneous recovery without any impact on adult life
options.D: Complete immunity to all forms of physical and mental illness

explanation: Correct! Without early help and intervention, young people in trouble with the law often grow up to become adult offenders. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T4#GNS225_U5_T4_h8)

question: What kind of data do quantitative research designs focus on?

options.A: Historical audio logs
options.B: Numerical data
options.C: Descriptive stories
options.D: Open-ended interviews

explanation: Remember: Quanti-tative = Quantities! This type of research relies heavily on numbers, measurements, and stats to break down variables. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T1#GNS224_U1_T1_h2)

question: A nurse wants to improve sanitation in a rural village. What is the best first step based on community empowerment principles?

options.A: Hold a town hall meeting to listen to community members discuss their main sanitation concerns
options.B: Write an academic paper about rural hygiene without visiting the village
options.C: Order all residents to clean their compounds under police supervision
options.D: Wait for international donors to build modern public toilets

explanation: Starting with dialogue ensures that the community leads the process and addresses problems they actually care about. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h7)

question: When did Nigeria introduce its first official National Drug Policy to fix chaotic drug distribution?
explanation: Nigeria rolled out its very first formal National Drug Policy back in 1990 to clean up unregulated drug imports and fight fake medicines. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T1#GNS215_U1_T1_h2)

question: Why do patients with untreated diabetes sometimes experience rapid weight loss?

options.A: Excessive fluid intake flushes away all dietary nutrients
options.B: High blood sugar levels speed up the normal metabolic rate
options.C: Kidneys filter out solid food particles into the urine
options.D: The body breaks down stored fat and muscle for energy

explanation: When glucose can't enter the cells for fuel, the body panics and starts burning its own fat and muscle instead, causing sudden weight loss. Makes total sense when you picture it! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T17#GNS324_U4_T17_h3)

question: What is the main difference between casual drug use and addiction?

options.A: Taking a prescribed cough syrup for a cold
options.B: Compulsive drug seeking despite harmful physical or social results
options.C: Using traditional herbs for malaria treatment
options.D: Drinking a single glass of wine at a family wedding

explanation: Addiction takes over a person's life, creating an unstoppable urge to find and use the drug even when it causes serious harm. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T11#GNS125_U2_T11_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a good lifestyle change for managing high blood pressure?

options.A: Engaging in regular aerobic exercise
options.B: Increasing dietary sodium intake
options.C: Stopping tobacco smoking completely
options.D: Limiting heavy alcohol consumption

explanation: More salt (sodium) holds onto water in the body and pushes blood pressure up—definitely something we want patients to cut back on! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T14#GNS214_U1_T14_h5)

question: What does a holistic approach mean in palliative care?

options.A: Addressing physical, emotional, and spiritual needs together
options.B: Focusing exclusively on spiritual counseling
options.C: Relying entirely on herbal remedies and local roots
options.D: Treating only the physical pain of the patient

explanation: A holistic approach looks at the *whole* person—body, mind, and spirit. We don't just treat a sore body; we care for the heart and mind too! [learn more](GNS321_U4_T2#GNS321_U4_T2_h2)

question: Why are lower doses of cytotoxic drugs used for autoimmune diseases compared to cancer?

options.A: Because autoimmune conditions heal on their own quickly
options.B: Because autoimmune cells are much weaker than cancer cells
options.C: To suppress immune activity without causing maximum cell kill
options.D: To prevent the drug from entering the bloodstream

explanation: Makes total sense! For autoimmune issues, we just want to calm the immune system down, not wipe out a whole tumor, so a smaller dose does the trick. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T7#GNS215_U6_T7_h3)

question: Why do many women in Nigeria end up using unsafe abortion methods?

options.A: Strict laws, social stigma, and poor access to safe care
options.B: Surgical facilities are cheap and everywhere
options.C: People just love traditional herbs more than hospitals
options.D: Primary health workers give very clear instructions

explanation: Fear of judgment, legal barriers, and a lack of friendly youth clinics push vulnerable people toward dangerous procedures. Great insight to keep in mind for clinical practice! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h1)

question: What is the key physical characteristic of marasmus compared to other forms of severe malnutrition?

options.A: Permanent yellowing of the eyes
options.B: Total paralysis of the lower limbs
options.C: Severe muscle wasting and a skeletal appearance
options.D: Sudden swelling of the face and belly

explanation: Marasmus results from severe lack of all calories, leading to extreme weight loss and muscle wasting without primary fluid retention. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h4)

question: When caring for someone with a physical disability, what is a major focus of addressing their social needs?

options.A: Eliminating the need for medical checkups and therapy
options.B: Restricting outdoor activities to prevent accidental falls
options.C: Ensuring complete cure of the underlying physical injury
options.D: Promoting meaningful connection and community belonging

explanation: You've got this! Social needs are all about human connection, inclusion, and feeling like you belong—not treating the medical condition itself. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T11#GNS225_U5_T11_h1)

question: What is the main goal of conducting regular stock audits on your ward?

options.A: To punish nurses who make simple documentation mistakes
options.B: To verify physical counts against records and ensure accountability
options.C: To remove all medical equipment from the clinical floor
options.D: To increase the purchase price of incoming medications

explanation: Audits aren't there to scare you! They help match what is actually on the shelf with your records, keeping everyone accountable and catching shortages early. [learn more](GST321_U4_T2#GST321_U4_T2_h7)

question: A client taking long-term NSAIDs for joint pain reports stomach upset and dark, tarry stools. What should you do first?

options.A: Advise the client to double the fluid intake immediately
options.B: Report the findings promptly to the healthcare provider
options.C: Suggest taking the medication on an entirely empty stomach
options.D: Reassure the client that dark stools are a normal side effect

explanation: Dark, tarry stools are a telltale sign of bleeding in the gut (GI bleed), a serious side effect of long-term NSAID use. Always report this right away! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T11#GNS222_U1_T11_h6)

question: Which complication is most directly linked to sluggish blood flow in the legs of an immobile patient?

options.A: Orthostatic hypotension
options.B: Deep vein thrombosis
options.C: Peripheral neuropathy
options.D: Pulmonary edema

explanation: Immobility slows venous return from the lower extremities, which allows blood clots to form more easily in deep veins. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T8#GNS324_U3_T8_h6)

question: What is the main difference between privacy and confidentiality in research?

options.A: Privacy relates to blood samples, while confidentiality is for interviews
options.B: Privacy is a person's right to control their space, while confidentiality is our duty to protect their data
options.C: Privacy is optional, but confidentiality is required by law
options.D: Privacy applies only to doctors, while confidentiality applies to nurses

explanation: Spot on! Privacy belongs to the patient's personal boundaries, while confidentiality is our professional promise to keep their secrets safe. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T19#GNS224_U1_T19_h4)

question: What is the main goal of performing a vulvar swab?

options.A: To measure the internal pH of the vaginal canal accurately
options.B: To collect microbial samples from the external female genitalia
options.C: To empty residual fluid from the urinary bladder completely
options.D: To remove excess tissue growth from the labia minora safely

explanation: You've got this! A vulvar swab is simply used to collect samples from the outside parts to find out what germ is causing issues like itching or unusual discharge. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h1)

question: During a neurological assessment, a nurse tests a patient's ability to feel light touch around the level of the umbilicus. Which dermatome is the nurse assessing?

options.A: T4
options.B: C5
options.D: L1

explanation: The tenth thoracic dermatome (T10) corresponds to the level of the umbilicus, making it a key landmark in spinal assessments. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T26#GNS211_U3_T26_h8)

question: Why is teaching safe body mechanics to family caregivers such an important nursing duty?

options.A: It cures chronic illnesses in the patient.
options.B: It protects the patient from falls and the caregiver from back injuries.
options.C: It cuts down the monthly grocery bill.
options.D: It gets rid of the need for grab bars.

explanation: You nailed it! Good lifting habits keep both the helper's back safe and the patient secure during transfers. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T5#GNS324_U3_T5_h6)

question: What is a major benefit of using rapid diagnostic tests like ELISA instead of traditional culture methods?

options.A: They yield results within hours instead of taking several days
options.B: They eliminate the need for any laboratory equipment or training
options.C: They guarantee that every single bacterium in the sample is killed
options.D: They only detect beneficial microbes and ignore harmful pathogens

explanation: Spot on! Rapid tests give answers in hours rather than days, which helps public health teams stop outbreaks fast without waiting around for slow cultures. [learn more](GST114_U5_T5#GST114_U5_T5_h6)

question: Why must basic physiological and safety needs be addressed before higher-level motivation?

options.A: Exhausted and unsafe workers cannot focus on professional growth
options.B: Labor laws forbid giving awards to hungry employees
options.C: Hospital management only cares about financial profits
options.D: Higher-level motivation is completely useless in nursing

explanation: Basic survival and safety form the foundation of human need; when staff are burnt out or underpaid, recognition alone fails to motivate them. [learn more](GST321_U1_T13#GST321_U1_T13_h5)

question: Which clinical sign will immediately make a doctor or nurse think of ordering a liver function panel?

options.A: Frequent coughing
options.B: Painful urination
options.C: Jaundice
options.D: Swollen ankles from heart failure

explanation: Spot on! That yellowing of the eyes and skin (jaundice) tells us bilirubin isn't clearing properly, making LFTs a top priority. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T11#GNS221_U2_T11_h4)

question: What is a potential long-term complication for an infant who survives a severe intracranial hemorrhage?

options.A: Developmental delays and seizure disorders
options.B: Early closure of all body joints
options.C: Permanent loss of the sense of smell only
options.D: Enlargement of the hands and feet

explanation: Significant bleeding inside the cranium can damage brain tissue, leading to chronic neurological issues like seizures and delayed milestones. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T16#GNS121_U6_T16_h6)

question: How do nurses use the idea of homeostatic imbalance when caring for patients?

options.A: To cure infections without using antibiotics by encouraging the patient to rest
options.B: To reverse genetic mutations that caused cellular metaplasia years ago
options.C: To connect abnormal vital signs and lab results to failing physiological control loops
options.D: To prevent the aging process from slowing down organ system functions

explanation: Spot on! When a patient's vital signs are out of whack, a good nurse sees it as a sign that the body's balancing loops are struggling and need help. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T10#GNS111_U1_T10_h7)

question: How does a fear of blame usually affect a nurse's problem-solving ability?

options.A: It improves the nurse's analytical and critical thinking skills
options.B: It encourages the nurse to report errors immediately
options.C: It causes the nurse to hide mistakes instead of fixing them
options.D: It helps the healthcare team work faster during emergencies

explanation: When people fear punishment, they tend to conceal errors rather than addressing the root problem openly. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T7#GNS112_U3_T7_h5)

question: What are the core parts of a genuine clinical apology?

options.A: A written legal contract signed by the hospital director
options.B: A medical justification explaining why the patient was at fault
options.C: Empathy, acknowledgment of harm, and sincere regret
options.D: Financial compensation and immediate resignation

explanation: A real apology means acknowledging what went wrong, showing true empathy, and expressing sincere regret for the pain caused. [learn more](GST319_U6_T3#GST319_U6_T3_h4)

question: Which of these is one of the most common causes of nursing malpractice claims?

options.A: Failing to attend annual hospital parties
options.B: Forgetting to log into the electronic health record on time
options.C: Medication administration errors
options.D: Refusing to work mandatory overtime shifts

explanation: Giving the wrong drug, wrong dose, or missing a route can easily harm a patient. This is why our 5 rights of medication administration are drilled into us! [learn more](GST322_U4_T9#GST322_U4_T9_h4)

question: When is a nurse researcher most likely to use a non-directional hypothesis?

options.A: When there is strong evidence supporting an increase
options.B: When the statistical software requires a one-tailed test
options.C: When little previous research exists on the topic
options.D: When the null hypothesis has already been proven true

explanation: If no one has studied the topic much before, you might not know which way things will go, so you keep it non-directional. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T10#GNS217_U3_T10_h4)

question: In safety management, what is considered the MOST effective way to deal with a hazard?

options.A: Using administrative policies
options.B: Conducting safety training
options.C: Elimination of the hazard
options.D: Wearing protective gloves

explanation: If you completely remove the danger, nobody can get hurt by it! That makes elimination the ultimate win in safety. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h2)

question: You just collected a wound swab from a patient with a leg ulcer. What's the best immediate step?

options.A: Place the swab inside a house refrigerator overnight to keep it cool
options.B: Send the specimen to the laboratory immediately in a proper transport container
options.C: Wash the cotton tip under running tap water to remove excess blood
options.D: Leave the capped tube on the nurse station desk until the end of the shift

explanation: Time is precious! Sending the sample straight away keeps fragile germs alive and stops normal skin bacteria from taking over. [learn more](GST114_U5_T4#GST114_U5_T4_h2)

question: How should a nurse apply a prescribed cream onto a patient's forearm?

options.A: Pat it into a thick pile and cover with tight gauze
options.B: Massage it hard until the skin turns bright red
options.C: Scrub it aggressively in circles to force deep penetration
options.D: Smooth it on gently in the direction of hair growth

explanation: Gentle, smooth strokes following hair growth prevent skin irritation, hair follicle inflammation, and unnecessary friction. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h7)

question: Why is infection control particularly challenging during home care procedures?

options.A: Household factors like pets and limited space increase contamination risks
options.B: Patients are immune to standard hospital-grade sanitizing agents
options.C: Sterile equipment cannot legally be brought into private residences
options.D: Water supplies in homes lack any form of bacterial filtration

explanation: Unlike sterile hospital rooms, homes contain everyday clutter, family members, and pets that make maintaining a clean field harder. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h4)

question: Which cranial nerve travels way past the neck to control organs in the chest and belly?

options.A: Optic nerve
options.B: Trigeminal nerve
options.C: Hypoglossal nerve
options.D: Vagus nerve

explanation: That's right! The vagus nerve is a wanderer (which is what 'vagus' means) that reaches down into the chest and abdomen to help run your internal organs. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h3)

question: Why do symptoms only show up a year after a person first gets infected?

options.A: The adult worm takes that long to migrate and approach the skin
options.B: The immune system suppresses all signs until the worm dies
options.C: The larvae remain dormant in the stomach for twelve months
options.D: The parasite only produces toxins after it leaves the human body

explanation: Exactly! The worm takes its sweet time growing and traveling through the body tissues before finally reaching the skin surface. Keep up the brilliant thinking! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h4)

question: As a nurse leader, why is it important to understand the psychology behind workplace changes?

options.A: To completely eliminate all feelings of stress in the hospital
options.B: To ensure that no clinical protocols are ever modified again
options.C: To view resistance as a normal reaction instead of laziness
options.D: To punish staff members who fail to adopt new policies

explanation: Spot on! When leaders understand this, they can approach staff hesitation with empathy and support rather than frustration. [learn more](GST319_U2_T5#GST319_U2_T5_h1)

question: What is the main abnormal type of haemoglobin found in sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: Haemoglobin S
options.B: Haemoglobin C
options.C: Haemoglobin A
options.D: Haemoglobin F

explanation: You nailed it! Haemoglobin S is the faulty protein that causes red blood cells to change shape when oxygen levels drop. Great start! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T8#GNS313_U3_T8_h1)

question: What is the main goal of tele-nursing?

options.A: Replacing all physical hospitals with apps
options.B: Manufacturing digital medical equipment
options.C: Diagnosing diseases without a doctor
options.D: Delivering nursing care using technology

explanation: Spot on! Tele-nursing simply means using tools like phones and video links to care for patients from a distance. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h1)

question: What is the main reason a nurse or doctor performs a thoracentesis for a pleural effusion?

options.A: To deliver continuous oxygen directly into the lung tissue
options.B: To permanently seal the pleural space against future leaks
options.C: To measure direct arterial blood pressure inside the thorax
options.D: To remove fluid for diagnostic analysis and relieve pressure

explanation: It's a win-win procedure: we take out some fluid so the lab can test it, and the patient instantly finds it easier to breathe. You're thinking like a real clinician! [learn more](GNS213_U2_T7#GNS213_U2_T7_h4)

question: A patient taking strong opioids long-term for cancer pain complains of terrible constipation. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Proactively give prescribed stool softeners and laxatives
options.B: Tell the patient to stop drinking fluids
options.C: Stop the opioid medication immediately without telling the doctor
options.D: Tell the patient that opioids never cause constipation

explanation: Spot on! Opioids slow down bowel movements significantly. Since our bodies don't build tolerance to this side effect, preventative laxatives are a nursing must-have! [learn more](GNS221_U3_T7#GNS221_U3_T7_h7)

question: Which action truly shows compassionate end-of-life nursing care for a dying patient at home?

options.A: Limiting family visits to ensure quiet hospital-like rules
options.B: Encouraging the patient to walk outside despite extreme weakness
options.C: Focusing strictly on lab test results and vital signs
options.D: Supporting family members and managing the patient's pain effectively

explanation: You got it! End-of-life nursing is all about easing physical pain and offering a warm, supportive shoulder to both the patient and their loved ones. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T1#GNS324_U3_T1_h8)

question: Where does a primary health clinic in Nigeria send its monthly injection safety report first?

options.A: The Local Government Area (LGA) focal officer
options.B: The international donor agency headquarters
options.C: The nearest private pharmaceutical distributor
options.D: Directly to the Federal Minister of Health

explanation: Correct! Reports start locally at the LGA level before moving upward to the state and federal tables. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h8)

question: What term is used when a reflex response is completely missing?

options.A: Autonomic dysreflexia
options.B: Neuromuscular fatigue
options.C: Hyperreflexia
options.D: Areflexia

explanation: Areflexia means the reflex is absent ('a-' meaning without). If it's just very weak, we call it hyporeflexia. You've got this! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T27#GNS211_U3_T27_h5)

question: What kind of thinking or belief is a classic sign of a patient with GPI?

options.A: Hearing strangers whispering secrets all day
options.B: Washing their hands constantly out of fear of germs
options.C: Being terrified of open spaces
options.D: Grandiose delusions, like believing they own the whole world

explanation: That's right! Patients with GPI often have huge, unrealistic beliefs about themselves, such as thinking they are multi-millionaires, royalty, or even gods. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T1#GNS222_U4_T1_h3)

question: How does your nursing focus shift when moving from emergency resuscitation to palliative care?

options.A: The focus shifts from invasive life-prolonging measures to symptom control and family support
options.B: The nurse stops all administration of pain medication
options.C: The nurse mandates that the patient be moved to a distant tertiary facility
options.D: The nurse stops visiting the patient entirely because no further treatment exists

explanation: End-of-life care is all about easing physical pain and wrapping the family in warm, compassionate support. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T13#GNS321_U2_T13_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of treating common diseases and minor injuries at a primary health center?

options.A: To practice advanced brain surgery on everyday patients
options.B: To keep patients admitted in bed for several weeks
options.C: To resolve health problems early and prevent dangerous complications
options.D: To replace all major regional hospitals in the country

question: Which gland gets the message from GnRH and then releases LH and FSH into the bloodstream?

options.A: The anterior pituitary
options.B: The hypothalamus
options.C: The adrenal gland
options.D: The posterior pituitary

explanation: Well done! The anterior pituitary gland acts on the hypothalamus's command to synthesize and pump out both LH and FSH. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T7#GNS121_U4_T7_h4)

question: Why do lab scientists often prefer molecular genetic tests over traditional culture methods for tricky microbes?

options.A: Genetic tests are always performed at the patient bedside by nurses
options.B: Molecular methods eliminate the need for any laboratory safety equipment
options.C: Culture methods cannot tell the difference between bacteria and viruses
options.D: Molecular methods identify organisms directly from genetic material without slow culture growth

explanation: Growing germs in a culture dish can take agonizingly days or weeks. Molecular tests find the DNA directly, giving quick answers when patients need care fast! [learn more](GST114_U1_T4#GST114_U1_T4_h6)

question: What makes paediatric nutrition different from adult nutrition?

options.A: Reducing total daily caloric intake
options.B: Preventing lifestyle diseases like hypertension
options.C: Supporting rapid growth and organ maturation
options.D: Maintaining a stable body weight over time

explanation: You've got this! Children grow fast and their organs are still developing, so they need special nutrients. Adults, on the other hand, mostly just need to maintain their weight. Keep up the great work! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T012#GNS227_U7_T012_h1)

question: What is the main danger of leaving clear units of measurement off a bar chart's axis?

options.A: The hospital will fail to meet basic fire safety codes
options.B: The chart software will crash and delete the saved file
options.C: Patients will refuse to take their prescribed medications
options.D: Readers may misinterpret the data and make poor clinical decisions

explanation: Without clear units, nobody can tell if the numbers represent counts, percentages, or money. Always label your axes! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T7#GNS217_U4_T7_h6)

question: What is a common inclusion criterion for admission to an adult day care home?

options.A: Mild to moderate functional decline requiring daytime supervision
options.B: Requirement for round-the-clock intensive surgical nursing
options.C: Comatose state requiring mechanical ventilation
options.D: Active and untreated infectious respiratory disease

explanation: Clients who need structured daytime support, socialization, or supervision while remaining at home at night are prime candidates for day care. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h3)

question: Why is it dangerous to put objects into the mouth of a seizing patient?

options.A: It increases the electrical voltage inside the brain
options.B: It triggers immediate cardiac arrest in all patients
options.C: It can damage teeth, cause oral trauma, or obstruct the airway
options.D: It permanently stops the postictal confusion phase

explanation: Trying to force items into a seizing patient's mouth often breaks teeth, hurts their gums, or blocks their breathing tube. Never put anything in their mouth! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T12#GNS222_U4_T12_h7)

question: What is the main way that most foodborne germs get into our bodies?

options.A: Vector-borne transmission
options.B: Fecal-oral route
options.C: Direct sexual contact
options.D: Airborne droplet route

explanation: It sounds unpleasant, but tiny, microscopic traces of waste pathogens find their way onto food or water and enter right through the mouth. Handwashing is our best defense! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T19#GNS313_U2_T19_h3)

question: A persistently high maternal mortality ratio in a specific region most strongly points to which underlying issue?

options.A: A cultural preference for giving birth during the rainy season
options.B: Weaknesses or failures within the local emergency healthcare system
options.C: An unusually high rate of twin and triplet births in the community
options.D: Excessive availability of free antenatal care medications

explanation: When maternal mortality stays high, it usually points to poor access to skilled birth attendants, delayed referrals, and inadequate emergency care. Recognizing this helps us know where to fix the system! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T016#GNS226_U1_T016_h2)

question: Why is it important to turn a vague thought into a specific, clear goal for a quality project?

options.A: It removes the need for nursing staff to collect data during shifts
options.B: It gives the team a clear target and defines how success will be measured
options.C: It guarantees that the project will cost zero Naira to implement
options.D: It prevents patients from asking questions about their care plan

explanation: A clear goal keeps everyone focused. When you know exactly what success looks like, it is much easier to reach it together! [learn more](GST319_U3_T3#GST319_U3_T3_h5)

question: What do we call a labour pattern where the cervix is opening slower than expected?

options.A: Protracted active phase
options.B: Normal progression
options.C: Prolonged latent phase
options.D: Precipitous labour

explanation: You got it! 'Protracted' just means delayed or sluggish. The cervix is dilating, but taking its sweet time. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T003#GNS226_U3_T003_h3)

question: Who is the focus of Tier 4 at the peak of the MHPSS pyramid?

options.A: Individuals with severe, disabling mental health conditions
options.B: Community volunteers organizing children's playgroups
options.C: People who simply need help finding food and clean water
options.D: Everyone living in a disaster-affected community

explanation: You're correct! Tier 4 is reserved for the smaller group of people who need specialized psychiatric care for severe mental health conditions. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T5#GNS314_U6_T5_h5)

question: What is the main difference between a patient's mood and their affect during a mental status exam?

options.A: Mood requires laboratory blood tests, while affect requires psychological tests
options.B: Mood only changes during sleep, while affect changes every single second
options.C: Mood is reported by the patient, while affect is observed outwardly by you
options.D: Mood is the observed facial expression, while affect is written in charts

explanation: Think of it this way: Mood is what the patient *tells* you they feel inside (like 'I feel sad'), whereas affect is how their emotions *look* to you on the outside (like crying or smiling). [learn more](GNS314_U1_T1#GNS314_U1_T1_h6)

question: Which part of the body is the main organ for managing heat exchange with the environment?

options.A: The kidneys
options.B: The lungs
options.C: The skin
options.D: The liver

explanation: You got this! The skin is our outer boundary, making it our primary tool for releasing or trapping body heat. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T4#GNS211_U2_T4_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a helpful question to ask when checking if a research study is good enough for your ward?

options.A: Can these findings actually work on our specific patient ward?
options.B: How many awards has the lead author won for writing?
options.C: Did the researchers use a good tool to measure the problem?
options.D: Was the number of patients large enough for good results?

explanation: Personal awards don't make science valid! We care about proper sample sizes, good measurement tools, and real clinical usefulness. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T26#GNS224_U1_T26_h7)

question: Why do non-communicable diseases (NCDs) like hypertension often go unnoticed for years?

options.A: Symptoms only appear after a person reaches retirement age
options.B: They develop silently in the body without immediate noticeable symptoms
options.C: Standard diagnostic laboratory tests cannot detect chronic illnesses early
options.D: Patients refuse to visit primary health centres for routine check-ups

explanation: Spot on! Conditions like high blood pressure creep up slowly without causing obvious pain or distress. That's why routine checks are so important for your patients. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T15#GNS313_U3_T15_h1)

question: What is the main goal of adaptive processes in our body and mind?

options.A: To eliminate all forms of emotional memory
options.B: To increase physical heart rate permanently
options.C: To prevent any future exposure to conflict
options.D: To restore internal balance during stress

explanation: Think of adaptive processes like your body's natural shock absorbers. They kick in to help you handle stress and bring your inner calm back! [learn more](GNS314_U2_T2#GNS314_U2_T2_h1)

question: What does self-medication mean in everyday healthcare?

options.A: Receiving free drug samples directly from a licensed hospital pharmacist
options.B: Sharing prescribed drugs strictly among family members living in the same house
options.C: Taking medications without a prescription from a qualified practitioner
options.D: Buying herbal teas from registered supermarkets for general wellness

explanation: Spot on! Self-medication simply means taking drugs without getting professional guidance or a valid prescription first. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T4#GNS215_U4_T4_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a daily job for a nurse in infection control?

options.A: Manufacturing the chemical disinfectants used in the hospital
options.B: Watching out for accidental breaks in sterile technique
options.C: Teaching patients how to wash their hands properly
options.D: Throwing away used needles safely in puncture-proof boxes

explanation: You got it! Factories make the chemical solutions; nurses are right at the bedside using them and keeping our patients safe. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h7)

question: What is the purpose of using Boolean operators like AND in a literature search?

options.A: To automatically translate foreign medical terms into English
options.B: To print research articles directly to the nurse station
options.C: To combine keywords and narrow down search results
options.D: To check if a website is legally safe to browse

explanation: Boolean operators help structure search queries so you retrieve articles specifically relevant to your exact clinical question. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h3)

question: Why is including a wide variety of foods in family meal planning so important?

options.A: It guarantees that every family member eats the exact same calorie count
options.B: It prevents nutrient gaps and avoids excessive intake of any single substance
options.C: It ensures the household spends the maximum possible food budget
options.D: It eliminates the need to provide clean drinking water at meals

explanation: Eating a diverse mix of foods makes it far more likely the body gets all necessary vitamins without relying too heavily on one food type. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T015#GNS227_U4_T015_h1)

question: What is the safest tool for a nurse to use when measuring liquid medicine for an infant?

options.A: A regular dining cup
options.B: A standard kitchen teaspoon
options.C: A calibrated oral syringe
options.D: An intravenous syringe

explanation: Household spoons vary wildly in size! A calibrated oral syringe gives us the exact, pinpoint accuracy needed to keep tiny babies safe. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T4#GNS125_U3_T4_h7)

question: Which nerve brings the parasympathetic signals that make the bladder contract when you want to pee?

options.A: Pudendal nerve
options.B: Obturator nerve
options.C: Hypogastric nerve
options.D: Pelvic nerve

explanation: Spot on! The pelvic nerve carries those important parasympathetic signals that tell the detrusor muscle to squeeze and empty the bladder. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T9#GNS121_U2_T9_h2)

question: What is the main use of a run chart in quality improvement?

options.A: To record patient medical diagnoses in an emergency
options.B: To schedule holiday shifts for nurses
options.C: To display data points over time and track performance trends
options.D: To calculate annual salaries for hospital staff

explanation: Spot on! Run charts plot data chronologically so you can see at a glance whether your ward's new interventions are actually improving things. [learn more](GST319_U1_T4#GST319_U1_T4_h7)

question: When does a health situation officially become an epidemic?

options.A: When case numbers suddenly rise above the normal expected baseline
options.B: When the causative organism is a drug-resistant bacteria
options.C: When it spreads to at least three different continents
options.D: When hospitals run out of basic treatment medications

explanation: You've got this! An epidemic happens when there is an unusual surge of cases in a community—basically, way more people falling sick than what healthcare workers normally expect to see. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T15#GNS313_U1_T15_h1)

question: What is the primary reason a newborn baby born to a diabetic mother often develops hypoglycemia shortly after birth?

options.A: The baby's high insulin production continues after the maternal glucose supply stops
options.B: The baby's liver is completely unable to produce any glycogen stores
options.C: Breast milk contains far too little sugar to nourish a large infant
options.D: The umbilical cord contains insulin-destroying enzymes

explanation: Inside the womb, the baby made extra insulin to handle the mother's high sugar. Once born, that high insulin level keeps working and quickly drops the baby's blood sugar too low. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T006#GNS226_U4_T006_h3)

question: What is a key part of preparing ahead of time for a home birth?

options.A: Educating the family on recognizing pregnancy danger signs
options.B: Booking a hospital bed just in case labor fails to start
options.C: Purchasing expensive medical monitors for the bedroom
options.D: Administering routine general anesthesia at 36 weeks

explanation: Knowledge is power! Teaching the family signs like heavy bleeding or severe headaches helps them call for help early if something goes wrong. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T7#GNS225_U3_T7_h3)

question: Why are community health nurses especially important for local mechanics, welders, and informal workers?

options.A: Informal workers never experience any health hazards on the job
options.B: Informal workers often lack formal safety training and access to corporate health clinics
options.C: Community nurses have direct authority to close down dangerous workshops
options.D: Informal workers are legally prohibited from visiting standard hospitals

explanation: Since informal workers don't have corporate safety clinics, community health nurses step in as their trusted source of health guidance. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T6#GNS225_U7_T6_h7)

question: A resident is scheduled for discharge next month. What should the care team arrange before departure?

options.A: Termination of all follow-up medical care
options.B: Immediate readmission to an acute psychiatric ward
options.C: Outpatient therapy appointments and secure housing
options.D: A police record check for employment eligibility

explanation: Wonderful! Good discharge planning means setting up safe housing and ongoing outpatient support beforehand to ensure a smooth transition and prevent relapse. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T4#GNS314_U5_T4_h8)

question: What happens during an 'ascending infection' in the female reproductive system?

options.A: Pathogens move upward from the vagina and cervix into the uterus and fallopian tubes
options.B: Viruses migrate from skin lesions down to the regional lymph nodes
options.C: Fungi multiply rapidly on the external vulva and travel to the bladder
options.D: Bacteria travel through the bloodstream directly to the heart valves

explanation: An ascending infection is just germs traveling upward—moving past the cervix and into the upper reproductive organs where they can cause serious trouble. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h2)

question: What does cost containment mean in healthcare?

options.A: Firing all senior nurses to replace them with students
options.B: Closing down hospital wards to save money on electricity
options.C: Reducing expenses without harming the quality of patient care
options.D: Refusing to treat patients who cannot pay cash immediately

explanation: Cost containment is about finding smart ways to save money while keeping patient outcomes safe and high quality. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h5)

question: Older adults often experience stiffer chest walls and weaker breathing muscles. What is the direct result of this?

options.A: Rapid expansion of lung capacity during exercise
options.B: Total elimination of carbon dioxide from the blood
options.C: Higher residual volume and reduced vital capacity
options.D: An immediate increase in total lung surface area

explanation: Think of it like an old rubber band—stiffer chest walls and weaker muscles mean older adults can't take as deep a breath, and they trap more air in their lungs (residual volume). [learn more](GNS324_U3_T2#GNS324_U3_T2_h2)

question: Why are advance directives so helpful in critical or end-of-life care?

options.A: They guarantee that the patient will recover fully
options.B: They guide medical treatment according to the patient's prior wishes
options.C: They eliminate all paperwork for the hospital staff
options.D: They give the doctor total control over all decisions

explanation: Advance directives let patients make their choices known ahead of time, taking the guesswork out of difficult situations. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T1#GNS221_U4_T1_h8)

question: Why do many patients with chronic kidney disease end up developing anemia?

options.A: The spleen removes healthy blood cells prematurely
options.B: The body destroys red blood cells too quickly
options.C: Dietary iron is no longer absorbed in the gut
options.D: Damaged kidneys fail to produce enough erythropoietin

explanation: You're learning fast! Since sick kidneys can't make enough EPO, the bone marrow doesn't get the signal to build new red blood cells, leading to anemia. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T8#GNS121_U2_T8_h2)

question: Why is transparency critical when mobilising a community for health action?

options.A: It stops villagers from asking questions about disease names
options.B: It guarantees that the federal government will send more funds
options.C: It builds lasting trust between the health team and the public
options.D: It prevents nurses from working long hours at the clinic

explanation: Open communication about goals, resources, and challenges removes suspicion and encourages people to cooperate fully. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T4#GNS124_U4_T4_h2)

question: What kind of diet is best for a patient recovering from enteric fever to protect their gut?

options.A: Soft, low-fiber diet
options.B: High-fiber whole grain diet
options.C: High-residue raw vegetable diet
options.D: Raw meat and dairy diet

explanation: Well done! A soft, low-fiber diet is gentle on the tummy and avoids irritating the healing intestinal walls. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T17#GNS313_U2_T17_h5)

question: What is a major difference between thoracic spinal nerves and the nerves in the neck or lower back?

options.A: Thoracic nerves only carry sensory information
options.B: Thoracic nerves do not connect to the spinal cord
options.C: Thoracic nerves do not form complex nerve plexuses
options.D: Thoracic nerves lack ventral roots

explanation: While other regions braid together into big webs (plexuses), thoracic nerves stay independent as clean, separate intercostal nerves between the ribs. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T26#GNS211_U3_T26_h6)

question: What good daily habit should nurses encourage patients to practice regarding bowel movements?

options.C: Holding bowel movements until bedtime
options.D: Straining forcefully every morning regardless of urge

question: Why is community involvement so important when trying to control disease reservoirs?

options.A: Community members are legally required to fund all government public health budgets
options.B: Local leaders must personally manufacture chemical pesticides and veterinary vaccines
options.C: Villagers need to conduct laboratory tests on captured rodents and vectors
options.D: Local residents must change daily habits like food storage and waste disposal for interventions to work

explanation: You're doing great! Public health measures only stick when everyday people change small daily habits to keep pests away. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T6#GNS313_U2_T6_h6)

question: What is the physical cause of Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)?

options.A: A bacterial infection destroying the tympanic membrane
options.B: Dislodged calcium crystals floating in the semicircular canals
options.C: Accumulation of cerumen deep in the inner ear canal
options.D: Chronic inflammation of the pharyngeal tonsils

explanation: Imagine tiny calcium crystals (otoconia) floating where they shouldn't be in your inner ear fluid. When you move your head, they drift and send dizzy, false motion signals to your brain! [learn more](GNS311_U3_T6#GNS311_U3_T6_h5)

question: Why is it a big mistake to make someone vomit after they swallow a corrosive chemical (like strong acid)?

options.A: It always causes permanent paralysis of the vocal cords
options.B: It forces the poison directly into the urinary bladder
options.C: It neutralizes all antidote medications given later in the hospital
options.D: It can cause additional severe burns to the esophagus as the chemical comes back up

explanation: Brilliant thinking! Corrosive chemicals burn on the way down, and forcing them back up means they burn the throat a second time. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T14#GNS221_U3_T14_h4)

question: Which routine lab test gives us a quick look at electrolytes like sodium and potassium?

options.A: Basic metabolic panel
options.B: Complete blood count
options.C: Liver function panel
options.D: Lipid profile test

explanation: Spot on! A BMP is your go-to lab panel for checking quick electrolyte and kidney numbers on the ward. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T11#GNS121_U2_T11_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a common driver of trauma in many Nigerian communities today?

options.A: Widespread technological automation
options.B: Farmer-herder conflicts
options.C: Insurgency and banditry
options.D: Displacement from homes

explanation: You got it! While things like insecurity, banditry, and displacement cause real trauma, office and factory automation aren't major drivers of community trauma here. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T1#GNS314_U6_T1_h4)

question: What should you do with the AED pads if the patient suddenly wakes up and starts breathing?

options.A: Move both pads to the patient's back to keep the skin warm
options.B: Peel them off immediately and throw them in the trash
options.C: Leave the pads attached to the chest in case arrest recurs
options.D: Wipe them down with bleach and pack them in the box

explanation: Leave the pads on! A recovered patient can still slip back into cardiac arrest very quickly, and you want the AED ready to go. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T2#GNS212_U2_T2_h7)

question: A depressed patient has lost ten pounds, looks pale, and is fatigued. What is the best initial nursing action?

options.A: Assume the weight loss is normal for depression and take no action
options.B: Perform a comprehensive nutritional assessment including a diet history and labs
options.C: Recommend an intense physical fitness gym membership to build muscle
options.D: Tell the patient to immediately start eating three large meals a day

explanation: Well done! A structured assessment helps us uncover specific nutritional deficits and physical health risks. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h4)

question: Why are transparent procurement rules so important in public health?

options.A: To ensure that all drugs are manufactured inside government hospitals
options.B: To remove the need for any financial auditing
options.C: To prevent inflated contract costs and substandard medical supplies
options.D: To allow doctors to bypass the budgeting process

explanation: Strict procurement rules stop corrupt contractors from overpricing items or supplying fake and substandard drugs to hospitals. [learn more](GST322_U3_T3#GST322_U3_T3_h5)

question: You are packing vaccines to take to a remote village for a community outreach day. What should you use to carry them?

options.A: Vaccine carrier with conditioned ice packs
options.B: An open plastic bucket with regular ice cubes
options.C: A large walk-in freezer unit
options.D: A cardboard box lined with newspapers

explanation: Vaccine carriers are portable and insulated, making them perfect for keeping your outreach supplies safe for a day out in the field. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T65#GNS214_U1_T65_h3)

question: How does an untreated lower genital infection turn into Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID)?

options.A: Fungi colonize the bladder wall and obstruct the normal flow of urine

options.C: Pathogens ascend from the cervix through the uterus into the fallopian tubes and pelvic cavity
options.D: Viruses alter bone marrow production, leading to severe immunological suppression

explanation: PID happens when bacteria travel upward from the vagina and cervix, causing widespread inflammation in the upper reproductive organs. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical chronic condition that threatens an older adult's independence?

options.A: Mild seasonal allergies
options.B: Diabetic nerve damage
options.C: Heart failure
options.D: Stroke

explanation: That's right! While allergies can be annoying, they don't cause long-term disability like major strokes, heart issues, or nerve damage do. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T5#GNS324_U3_T5_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of Psychological First Aid (PFA) for someone who has gone through trauma?

options.A: Prescribe heavy psychiatric drugs for sedation
options.B: Force the individual to retell their trauma details
options.C: Provide long-term psychoanalysis and deep therapy
options.D: Offer humane, supportive, and practical assistance

explanation: PFA is all about being a calming, supportive presence. You don't need to be a psychiatrist; you just offer practical comfort and safety without forcing people to retell scary stories. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T21#GNS225_U5_T21_h4)

question: Which quick screening tool do healthcare workers use to check for problem drinking?

options.A: Braden scale
options.B: Apgar score chart
options.C: CAGE questionnaire
options.D: Glasgow Coma Scale

explanation: The CAGE questionnaire is a short, simple set of four questions used to spot lifetime alcohol problems. Easy to remember! [learn more](GNS125_U2_T11#GNS125_U2_T11_h6)

question: What is the name of the primary federal legislation that guides quarantine enforcement in Nigeria?

options.A: The Quarantine Act
options.B: The Epidemic Control Code
options.C: The National Health Insurance Act
options.D: The Nursing and Midwifery Decree

explanation: The Quarantine Act is the established legal framework empowering Nigerian authorities to manage public health borders and restrictions. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h3)

question: What is the main goal of using research in nursing?

options.A: Applying scientific findings to improve bedside patient care
options.B: Writing and publishing new papers in medical journals
options.C: Cutting the cost of hospital drugs and equipment
options.D: Complying with strict hospital administrative rules

explanation: You've got this! Research utilization is simply about taking proven science and using it right at the bedside to give our patients the best care possible. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T3#GNS224_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why should you NEVER use a patient's room number to verify who they are?

options.A: Doctors change room assignments every single hour
options.B: Room numbers are often painted the same color
options.C: Patients frequently switch rooms or beds
options.D: Hospital charts do not display room numbers

explanation: Beds and rooms change all the time in a busy ward. Location is never a safe way to identify a patient! [learn more](GNS125_U3_T1#GNS125_U3_T1_h5)

question: What is the main goal when public health workers investigate a sudden disease outbreak?

options.A: To punish individuals who failed to maintain hygiene
options.B: To document medical billing records for the hospital
options.C: To manufacture new vaccines for the infected population
options.D: To find the exact source and stop the outbreak from spreading

explanation: Detective work is a huge part of nursing! Finding the source quickly lets health teams step in and protect the rest of the community. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T7#GNS313_U1_T7_h5)

question: Your patient starts coughing uncontrollably and gets short of breath during a tube feeding. What's the most likely issue?

options.A: Normal adjustment to the tube
options.B: Accidental pulmonary aspiration
options.C: Esophageal stricture formation
options.D: Metabolic acidosis from fluid overload

question: Why is active listening an important skill in health promotion?

options.A: It helps the nurse uncover barriers stopping the patient from being healthy
options.B: It replaces the need to check vital signs or physical health
options.C: It shortens the time required for documentation paperwork
options.D: It guarantees the patient will never develop a chronic illness

explanation: Listening carefully lets nurses find out if fear, cost, or confusion is getting in the way of a patient's care. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h5)

question: What is the primary goal of microbial identification in a clinical setting?

options.A: To count the total number of human cells in a clinical sample
options.B: To measure the patient's exact blood pressure and pulse rate
options.C: To sterilize medical equipment before a surgical procedure
options.D: To determine the exact pathogen causing an infection for targeted treatment

explanation: Knowing the specific organism allows healthcare providers to choose the most effective and narrow-spectrum treatment possible. [learn more](GST114_U5_T3#GST114_U5_T3_h1)

question: Why is continuous reassessment so important in critical care nursing?

options.A: Initial assessments are usually completely incorrect
options.B: Doctors refuse to read reports written only once
options.C: Hospital management requires hourly computer entries
options.D: Patient conditions can change rapidly and unpredictably

explanation: In critical care, a patient who looks calm right now could take a turn for the worse minutes later. That's why we never stop checking! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T2#GNS321_U2_T2_h9)

question: What is another popular name for schistosomiasis?

options.A: River blindness
options.B: Chagas disease

question: Why is buying vegetables that are currently "in season" a smart strategy?

question: What is the term for the age-related loss of muscle mass and strength?

question: Why do clinics keep a 'buffer stock' of essential drugs?

question: Within how many hours must Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) be started to work effectively?

question: What typically happens to the risk of early marriage during wars, displacement, or natural disasters?

question: Why do babies and young children dehydrate so quickly when they have an illness like diarrhea?

question: Why must honey be strictly avoided for infants under one year of age?

question: A public health nurse visits a crowded urban settlement to improve sanitation and teach hygiene. Whose historical footsteps is this nurse following?

question: Why do doctors request sensitivity testing before starting targeted antibiotic treatment?

question: What happens to nutrients during metabolism after your body absorbs them?

options.C: They are used for immediate energy or stored for later use

question: What is the primary purpose of a community health nursing care plan?

options.D: To serve as a decoration for the office wall of the clinic head

question: A nurse provides a targeted stress management program specifically for children whose parents are going through a bitter divorce. What type of intervention is this?

question: How can severe arthritis make mealtime a struggle for a home care patient?

question: What are the folds inside the vaginal wall called that allow for stretching?

question: During a community health outreach in a rural Nigerian village, a nurse notices grandmothers defending FGM as a sign of purity. What is the most effective initial approach for the nurse?

question: What is osteomyelitis?

question: What is the main reason doctors order a skin snip test?

question: Why is it important to monitor pressure and volume during mechanical ventilation?

question: What is a major risk when a country relies too heavily on international aid for its health care?

question: What is the main thing that separates a true experiment from a quasi-experiment?

question: If someone has a family history of anxiety, what role does a major life stressor play?

question: Why is open dumping of raw, untreated medical waste a terrible practice?

question: A patient with severe burn wounds is at risk of poor healing if which nutritional goal is missed?

question: Which scenario is an example of acquiring passive immunity?

question: What shows that your discharge teaching for a stroke caregiver was truly effective?

options.B: Performing complex elective surgeries in rural primary health centers
options.C: Delivering life-saving interventions outside traditional hospital intensive care units
options.D: Managing chronic stable illnesses during routine home visits

explanation: You don't always need a big hospital ICU to save a life! Community critical care is all about bringing quick emergency help right to primary clinics and homes. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T13#GNS321_U2_T13_h1)

question: What kind of work environment destroys long-term quality improvement?

options.A: A workplace with too many staff meetings
options.B: An environment that uses electronic medical records
options.C: A hospital that provides regular free training
options.D: A toxic or purely punitive work environment

explanation: Fear of punishment stops staff from reporting errors or speaking up about why a new protocol is failing. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h3)

question: What makes a nutrient 'essential'?

options.A: It is only found in expensive dietary supplements.
options.B: The body cannot make it, so it must come from food.
options.C: The body produces it in massive quantities daily.
options.D: It provides zero calories but tastes sweet.

explanation: If our bodies can't manufacture it on their own, it's 'essential' that we eat it. Simple as that! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T001#GNS227_U1_T001_h4)

question: Why is it important for community nurses to understand local cultural beliefs and traditional practices?

options.A: Traditional practices completely replace the need for scientific training
options.B: Cultural beliefs strongly influence health-seeking behaviors and treatment delays
options.C: Government laws forbid the use of modern medicine in rural areas
options.D: Nurses are required to participate in traditional festival dances

explanation: Spot on! People often visit traditional healers first when sick. Understanding their views helps nurses build trust and encourage safe, timely care. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T7#GNS225_U1_T7_h7)

question: Why is organizing raw patient data important in nursing informatics?

options.A: It eliminates all documentation duties for staff nurses
options.B: It ensures that patients never experience medication errors
options.C: It completely replaces the need for direct physical assessment
options.D: It turns data into useful information for clinical decisions

explanation: Raw data alone is not helpful until it is organized and analyzed to guide safe, effective patient care choices. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T2#GNS113_U1_T2_h1)

question: What is the very first nursing priority when caring for a patient who is heavily intoxicated?

options.A: Asking the patient to sign a treatment contract
options.B: Maintaining airway, breathing, and circulation
options.C: Exploring childhood causes of substance use
options.D: Teaching about the long-term dangers of drugs

explanation: Correct! Always remember your ABCs first. Keeping the patient breathing and stable is always our top emergency priority before anything else. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T5#GNS223_U6_T5_h6)

question: What is another common name for incidence density?

options.A: Cumulative prevalence
options.B: Point mortality rate
options.C: Person-time incidence
options.D: Case fatality ratio

explanation: Incidence density is also known as person-time incidence because it tracks the actual time units each person contributes to the study. You're mastering the terminology! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h5)

question: Why is tele-nursing especially helpful for rural healthcare in Nigeria?

options.A: It lets nurses care for patients without forcing long, costly travel
options.B: It eliminates all expenses related to purchasing medical equipment
options.C: It guarantees uninterrupted electricity supply in remote villages
options.D: It completely replaces the need for physical hospitals everywhere

explanation: Spot on! Many patients in rural areas spend a lot of money and time just getting to a clinic. Tele-nursing brings basic nursing advice directly to them. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T7#GNS113_U3_T7_h1)

question: Why is building trust with the community so important for a nurse?

options.A: It legally protects the nurse from medical malpractice lawsuits
options.B: It encourages community members to accept immunizations and report illnesses early
options.C: It eliminates the need for any environmental sanitation work
options.D: It guarantees financial funding from international donors

explanation: Spot on! People are much more likely to listen, take their vaccines, and share health worries when they know and trust their nurse. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T16#GNS313_U1_T16_h8)

question: According to the Hoehn and Yahr scale, what does Stage 1 Parkinson's disease mean?

options.A: Symptoms are limited to one side of the body with minimal disability.
options.B: Bilateral disease is present with severe impairment of balance.
options.C: Symptoms are completely absent during physical exertion.
options.D: The patient is confined strictly to a wheelchair or bed.

explanation: Stage 1 is the very beginning of the journey. The symptoms affect only one side of the body (unilateral) and cause very little disruption to daily life. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T4#GNS222_U4_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of a post-disaster debriefing or hot wash session?

options.A: Calculating annual bonuses for hospital administrators
options.B: Analyzing what went well and where emergency processes failed
options.C: Assigning blame to individual nurses who made mistakes
options.D: Destroying all medical records from the disaster period

explanation: Debriefings review the response objectively so the healthcare team can learn and improve for future emergencies. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h8)

question: Which hormone does the pineal gland release to help you sleep?

options.A: Thyroxine
options.B: Cortisol
options.C: Melatonin
options.D: Insulin

explanation: You nailed it! The pineal gland pumps out melatonin when it gets dark to help your body wind down for sleep. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T19#GNS211_U3_T19_h4)

question: A patient with bad food poisoning keeps throwing up and cannot keep any water down. What is your next best step?

options.A: Force the patient to drink large volumes of water
options.B: Withhold all fluids for the next 48 hours
options.C: Administer strong oral laxatives immediately
options.D: Initiate prescribed intravenous fluid therapy

explanation: If the mouth isn't an option because of constant vomiting, setting up an IV line is the safest way to get fluids and electrolytes back into their system. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T19#GNS313_U2_T19_h6)
